    Precision features for meta-analytic models

    Source: R/recipes-steps.R
    step_meta_precision.Rd

    step_meta_precision() creates a specification of a recipe step that turns sampling variances (or standard errors) into precision features: the standard error ("sei"), the precision \(1/SE\) ("precision") or the inverse variance weight \(1/(v + \tau^2)\) ("weight"). Standard errors and variances are the predictors of Egger and PET-PEESE type models of small-study effects.

    Usage

    step_meta_precision(
  recipe,
  ...,
  input = c("vi", "sei"),
  output = "sei",
  tau2 = 0,
  role = "predictor",
  trained = FALSE,
  columns = NULL,
  keep_original_cols = TRUE,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = recipes::rand_id("meta_precision")
)

# S3 method for class 'step_meta_precision'
tidy(x, ...)

    Arguments

    recipe

    A recipe object. The step will be added to the sequence of operations for this recipe.

    ...

    One or more selector functions to choose the variance (or standard error) columns. See recipes::selections().

    input

    Are the selected columns sampling variances ("vi") or standard errors ("sei")?

    output

    One or more of "sei", "precision" and "weight".

    tau2

    Between-study variance added to the variances for "weight". Use 0 for common-effect weights.

    role

    The role of the new columns. Defaults to "predictor"; use recipes::update_role() to make the effect size an outcome.

    trained

    A logical to indicate if the quantities for preprocessing have been estimated.

    columns

    A character vector of the selected columns. This is NULL until the step is trained by recipes::prep().

    keep_original_cols

    Keep the input columns?

    skip

    A logical. Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by recipes::bake()?

    id

    A character string that is unique to this step to identify it.

    x

    A step_meta_precision object.

    Value

    An updated version of recipe with the new step added. The new columns are named <column>_<output>. tidy() returns a tibble with columns terms, output and id.

    See also

    Other recipe steps: step_meta_effect_size(), step_meta_impute_sd()

    Examples

    library(recipes)
bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
rec <- recipe(.yi ~ .vi + ablat, data = bcg) |>
  step_meta_precision(.vi, output = c("sei", "weight"))
bake(prep(rec), new_data = NULL)
